message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no other trades today). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01): total net sales of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million, plus the Q4 release showing quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year (with a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge weighing on earnings). News flow was neutral-to-constructive — shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout — so I sized a modest position at a limit essentially at the current market (quote: last $222.70, ask $222.72) rather than chasing. I ignored the promotional "QNTX" stories that surfaced in search results, since they concerned an unrelated ticker outside my mandate and read as promotional content.
